title: Sweet potato casserole
subtitle: American Thanksgiving sweet potato bake with pecan crumble
excerpt: Mashed sweet potato enriched with butter, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla, baked in a dish and topped with a brown-sugar-and-pecan streusel. The centrepiece Thanksgiving side dish across the American South and Midwest.
sourceNotes: Sweet potato casserole is a Thanksgiving staple documented throughout Southern and Midwestern American cooking from the late nineteenth century. The pecan-crumble version (as opposed to the marshmallow-topped version) is most prominent in African-American and Southern cooking texts and in modern community cookbooks. The marshmallow-topped version dates from 1917, when Angelus Marshmallows published a recipe book featuring it.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the sweet potato base up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Add the topping and bake just before serving.

content.text: Sweet potato casserole sits in a curious zone between a vegetable dish and a dessert, and it is not apologetic about this. The sweet potato filling is enriched with butter, eggs, vanilla, and brown sugar, and it bakes into something between a soufflé and a pudding. The pecan-and-brown-sugar crumble on top adds a bitter-sweet crunch that makes the whole thing work. It is Thanksgiving food.

items.prepNote: about 4 large, peeled, cut into chunks

content.text: Boil the sweet potato chunks in well-salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until completely tender. Drain thoroughly and allow to steam-dry for 5 minutes. Mash until smooth.

Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Beat the butter and brown sugar into the sweet potato. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in the vanilla, milk, and salt until smooth. Pour into a buttered baking dish.
Mix the crumble topping ingredients together and scatter evenly over the surface. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is golden and the filling is just set with a slight wobble in the centre.

items.cause: Sweet potato not drained and dried thoroughly
items.fix: After draining, return the sweet potato to the pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes to drive off excess moisture before mashing.

content.text: Sweet potato casserole is the Thanksgiving side dish that American families argue about. The marshmallow camp and the pecan camp represent a genuine regional divide. The marshmallow version is more Northern and Midwestern. The pecan version is more Southern. Both trace to the late nineteenth century, when sweet potatoes were a staple crop of the American South. In many Southern African-American families, this dish is as central to Thanksgiving as the turkey.
